channel.title: Khayt for macOS
channel.description: Updates for the native Khayt Mac app.

item.title: 4.0.0-beta.43
item.description:
*Khayt for macOS only. The Windows and Linux app is on its own version — see [VERSIONING.md](https://github.com/KhaytApp/Khayt/blob/main/VERSIONING.md).*
This release holds an update that carries "Before you update" items until they are read, before the download and again at the first start; adds Settings ▸ General ▸ Internet use and "Make no internet calls", which a paired owner's phone can also switch; shows what earlier scans found in Find printers; lets a paired phone carry a role that the Mac enforces on every request; signs the update feed when a release is published; and fixes four findings of the release review.
### Added
- **Mac: an update that has "Before you update" items is held until they are read.** When Khayt finds such an update (or one that skips over a release that has them), a sheet opens over the window first, "An update is ready": the items, in the shop's language, a tick box "I have read these changes", then **Continue to the update** and **Later**. Continue opens the usual update window, which downloads and installs as before; Later records nothing and the sheet returns at the next check. Until the tick, the update cannot be reached another way: **Check for Updates…** opens this sheet first, and the updater itself refuses the version. What was read here is not asked again at the first start after the update; anything the new app lists that this sheet did not show, or showed in other words, still is. **Check for Updates…** with nothing new now reliably says so: the window it opens waits until the updater is free, where before the request could be dropped. The items come from the new release itself (`release-gates.json`, which `mac/release-local.sh` now attaches to every Mac release), read under the Updates line of "Internet use". If they cannot be read (a release from before this, no connection), the update is offered as before and the first-start sheet shows them instead: an update is never blocked by a file that is missing. Anyone signed in may tick, not only the owner.
- **Mac: after an update that has "Before you update" items, Khayt shows them at the first start and waits until they are read.** A sheet over the window, "Khayt was updated": which version this Mac runs now and which it ran before, the items of every such release in between (newest first, each said once), and "I have read these changes". Continue stays off until that is ticked, and there is no Later: the update is already installed. With the staff lock on it comes after sign-in, and whoever signs in may continue. A new install is asked nothing. A Mac updating from before this sheet existed is shown beta.42's item once, even if it read it in the release notes. The Mac's update window used to show these items as plain release notes and hold nothing. The rule is the Windows/Linux app's own (`lib/launch-gate.js`), and the items ship inside the app (`lib/release-gates.json`, which the Mac's release script now refuses to build without). Drawn from page 28, frame B, signed off Nov 23.
- **Mac: Settings ▸ General ▸ Internet use.** The page for the switch that stops Khayt calling the internet (Figma page 27).
- **Mac: Find printers shows what earlier scans found.** A printer that was asleep or busy during the few seconds of a scan used to be simply missing. The sheet now lists it under "Seen earlier, not in this scan", with when it was last seen ("Seen 2 hours ago. It may be asleep or busy.") and, if its address has moved, where it was before. Add works on it as on any found printer, after asking first: it did not answer this scan, and its address may belong to something else by now. A line says the list is kept on this computer only, for three days, and "Forget earlier finds" empties it. With nothing seen earlier the sheet is as it was. Drawn from page 28, frame A, signed off Nov 23.
- **Mac: the update feed is signed when a release is published (first of two steps; nothing is required yet).** The archive was already signed, so nobody could make a Mac install something Khayt did not publish. The feed that announces updates was not: whoever could alter it could change the notes a Mac shows before an update, or offer it a build that is not the latest. (It does not stop an update being hidden: an old signed feed still verifies.) Both publish lanes (`mac-publish.yml`, `mac-release.yml`) now sign the feed with the key that signs the archive, check it with Sparkle's own verify, with `scripts/mac-appcast-verify.js` against the key inside the app being shipped, and as well-formed XML (the checker needs only the public key and can check the live feed: `node scripts/mac-appcast-verify.js --url https://khaytapp.com/mac/appcast.xml`), and do this before the release is made public. Installed Macs read a signed feed exactly as they read today's. The app does not require the signature yet; that is the release after the first signed one has been seen to update a real Mac. The release notes shown in the update window now come from inside the feed (the release's CHANGELOG section) and not from the GitHub release page, because a required signature covers the notes too and that page cannot be signed; the page stays as "Version History". **After a cut, nothing may edit `mac/appcast.xml` in the website repo by hand: any changed byte breaks the signature.**
- **Shared core (Mac and iPhone): a printer's success rate can be worked out natively, by the desktop's own rule.** `lib/printer-success.js` is now in KhaytCore's bundle. `KhaytEngine.successRates(orders:machines:from:to:calendar:)` returns each printer's finished, failed, cancelled and unknown runs, its rate, and whether there are enough decided runs to show one (`successRunsNeeded()`, five); with a calendar, each run counts on that calendar's own day (the book's, through daylight-saving changes too), not the UTC day. `KhaytEngine.successPercent(_:)` gives the whole per cent every app shows, where 199 of 200 reads 99 and never 100. Nothing on screen changes here: the iPhone's "Success rate" line and the Mac's Machine profit read it. Held to the vectors the Windows/Linux app's own test runs.
- **Mac: the owner's phone can read which phones are paired, and whether prices show in the slicer.** Two read-only routes on the native Mac's LAN server, for the iPhone: `GET /api/devices` lists the shop's paired phones (name, role, paired with the PIN or by number, last seen, and which one is asking), and `GET /api/devices/connectors` gives the shop's "Show prices in the slicer" switch and each paired slicer's grant. Owner only: a signed phone whose role is owner, never the PIN alone, an API token or a manager's phone. No key, PIN tag or anything that could enrol or impersonate a device is in either answer, and both are signed. Nothing can be changed through them.
- **Mac, German: the Preferences pane is "Präferenzen".** It was "Einstellungen", the same word as the Settings window it sits in, so its path read "Einstellungen ▸ Einstellungen". "Voreinstellungen" already means presets, so it is "Präferenzen", as on Windows and Linux.
- **Mac: an owner's phone can turn "Make no internet calls" on or off.** `POST /api/network/switch` on the Mac's LAN server, for a signed phone whose role is owner. It is the Mac's own change by the same path: the same forward-only stamp, the same "tell my other computers" call, one write, and the Mac stops or starts at once. A stale tap (the switch changed since the phone last looked) changes nothing and says what is true now. The answer is signed, so the phone shows "Done" only when the Mac really said so, and `/api/devices/self` tells an owner's phone the route is there (`can: ["network-switch"]`). Documented in `docs/LAN_API.md`; the desktop does not serve it yet.
- **Mac: when your other computers could not be told that internet use is back on because this Mac's Khayt Cloud sign-in ended, it says so and offers Sign in again.** On Settings ▸ General ▸ Internet use, under the switch: "Internet use was turned back on here, but your other computers don't know yet.", who turned it on and when, and one button that opens the Khayt Cloud sign-in. Khayt keeps the change and sends it by itself once somebody signs in. Before, the Mac only knew the change had not been sent, not why, so it could not say what to do. Shown to somebody who may change the switch; it goes when the change is sent, when the shop stops sharing the switch, or when a newer setting replaces it. Drawn from frame H, signed off Nov 23.
- **Mac: only a computer that hears the printers publishes them to Khayt Cloud.** Khayt Cloud keeps one live picture per shop, and every unlocked computer of the shop could replace it. An owner's laptop at home, which cannot reach the printers, published "not heard" for all of them every 45 seconds, so the phone flipped between the real printers and nothing; a Mac whose polling had stopped kept saying "Printing 42%". The Mac now publishes only while at least one printer answered it in the last three minutes, and is silent otherwise. The rule is the shared `lib/live-snapshot.js` (`hasFreshPoll`), and the Mac now asks that file for what a snapshot holds, what counts as a change and when one is due, where it had its own Swift copy.
- **Mac: a paired phone learns the shop's "make no internet calls" switch from `/api/status`.** A phone in a floor role (operator, viewer) has no copy of the book, so it could not know. A status request signed by a paired device now also gets `network: {offline, keep}`, read by the shared rule, and the answer is signed back so nothing on the Wi-Fi can tell the phone the switch is off. Everyone else gets the same public counts as before.
- **Mac: `khayt://plugin/install?id=…&version=…`, the directory's "Install in Khayt" link.** The link names a connector and a version and nothing else. Khayt reads its own signed index, checks that it lists that connector at that version and has not withdrawn it, downloads the manifest from where the index says, checks the bytes are the ones the index promised and that Khayt signed them, and opens the same consent sheet as a hand install, in Settings ▸ Integrations. Nothing is installed until the shop presses Install there, so a web page cannot pre-tick, skip or soften consent. A link with any other field (an address, a second id), an id that is not a connector id or a version that is not a version is not a link at all. Only somebody who may change settings, in a window that can save, gets the sheet; otherwise a sentence says why and that nothing was installed. 7 new strings in 9 languages. Tests: the link's shape, the happy path writing nothing, every refusal (unsigned or expired index, unlisted, another version, withdrawn, wrong bytes, an unsigned manifest, a mismatched id), and the lock.
- **Mac: the switch through Khayt Cloud, three follow-ups.**
- **Mac: "Use the newer setting" reads the newer setting when this Mac does not hold it.** When the owner changes the switch at the same moment as another computer, and what the other computer set could not be read (the read failed, or Khayt was restarted), pressing "Use the newer setting" now makes one read from Khayt Cloud itself, even while the shop's switch is on here, and applies what it reads. If Khayt Cloud cannot be reached, the question stays and says so; if Khayt Cloud holds no setting, or the setting cannot be saved, the question stays and says that. Before, the press cleared the question with nothing applied, and this Mac stayed offline with no call it could make to hear the switch again. The read is never made under "Also on this Mac only". 3 new strings in 9 languages.
- **Mac: the two questions about the shop's switch, and its row, as signed off.**
- **Mac: "Also tell my other computers through Khayt Cloud" now does it.** The option on Settings ▸ General ▸ Internet use is shown now that its call is wired. It is off unless the owner turns it on.
- **Mac: the install count and the crash and usage opt-ins are the owner's to change under the staff lock** (decided Nov 22; the desktop did the same in #2636). With the lock off, anyone can, as before.
- **Mac: every call the app makes to the internet now asks one switch first (no screen yet).** The rule is the shared `lib/outbound.js`; the Mac asks it where each request is built, by what the call is for.
- **Mac: a phone can tell how old a printer's picture is, and why it stopped answering, in any language.** `/api/machines/live` rows gain `lastOkAt` (when the printer last ANSWERED; `lastUpdated` moves on a failed poll too), `errorCode` (one word no language changes: `access-refused`, `http`, `not-set-up`, `certificate`, `unreadable`, `unreachable`) and `httpStatus`. `error` stays the sentence in the shop's language. Documented in `docs/LAN_API.md` for the desktop to match.
- **A finished print remembers what was in each head.** When Khayt notes how much filament each head used, it now also stamps that head's colour and material as read just after that print ended: from the spool's RFID tag when the printer read one, otherwise from what the printer reports as loaded, or what was typed on the machine (`colourFrom: "rfid"` or `"loaded"`). The job keeps saying "black PLA" after the spool is changed. A head nobody can name gets no colour, nothing is guessed, and jobs already written are left as they are. The rule is `lib/printer-actuals.js headColour`; the Mac reads the tags with one more read-only request after the print ends.
- **Mac: the rest of printer batches 2 and 3, with no new screens.**
- **Mac: the Send sheet says whether the file fits the bed.** The checks now read where the file's models sit from the slicer's own object outlines (`lib/gcode-placed-extents.js`: Klipper's `EXCLUDE_OBJECT_DEFINE`, which OrcaSlicer and the Snapmaker U1's files carry, or PrusaSlicer's `objects_info`). A file that fits shows "Fits the bed: 182 × 140 mm on 270 × 270 mm". One too big or too tall holds the send, with the sizes. A file with no object list is judged from its moves only when the Mac read the whole file (up to 32 MB), and then it only warns, because a skirt or a purge line is in the moves. A larger file with no object list has no bed row. 1 new string in 9 languages.
- **Mac: printer batch 1 — checks before a send, printers as their own role area, and seven state chips.** Figma: Mac file, page 23.
- **Mac: the screens for pairing a phone by code, with a role.** Figma: Mac file, page 26, signed off Nov 22. Settings ▸ Online.
- **Mac: a phone that cancels pairing by code tells the Mac.** `DELETE /api/devices/pair/<pairId>` with the phone's poll secret ends its own request, so the Mac goes back to waiting at once and no longer shows a number nobody is looking at until the window ends. Only the phone that asked can cancel, an approval already given is not undone, and the offer stays counted.
- **Mac: Find printers remembers what it found.** Each scan the owner starts adds what it saw to a short list kept on that Mac, outside the book: one entry per printer, three days, forty at most, by the shared rule (`lib/found-printers.js`). It is the same file the Windows/Linux app keeps, so a Mac running both shares one list. Nothing shows it yet: the picker with earlier finds waits for its frame.
- **Mac: each printer's problems and waiting reasons, worked out by the shared rules and sent to the phone and the cloud.** After every sweep the Mac asks `lib/printer-problems.js` what each printer says is wrong and `lib/waiting-at-machine.js` whether it waits for a person, and adds `problems` and `waiting` to every printer on `/api/machines/live` and in the cloud's live snapshot. The phone only decodes them. A Snapmaker U1 is asked for two more status objects in the read it already gets (its exception list and power-loss flag), only when the printer itself lists them, so a runout names its head and a power loss is said (information only: Khayt never sends resume or discard). A printer that is not answering has no live problems, but a finished print whose bed was not cleared still shows as waiting, because that is read from what is stored. `rfid-tray` and `timelapse-attach` are bundled for the screens that follow their frames; nothing calls them yet. No new screens on the Mac. After a finished print on a job the book names, the Mac also reads the U1's history once (a read) and notes how much filament each head used on the job (`actualHeads`, split by the shared rule in proportion to the slicer's per-head figures and marked `proportional`). The printer's own job id is the key, so a print is never recorded twice, by this Mac, the desktop or a second look. Tests: the 15 problem vectors and 11 waiting vectors through the Mac's engine, the needs per printer, and the live row.
- **Mac: a paired phone can say a bed is clear.** `POST /api/printer/{machineId}/bed-clear` is the phone's "Bed is clear" and "Taken off". It writes what the Mac's own "Bed is clear" button writes, `bedClearedAt` on the machine, through one shared function, so the dispatcher may offer that printer again and the "print to take off" line ends. Signed, enrolled phones only; the role rule (`lib/device-roles.js`) asks for `machines:control`, so an operator, a manager or the owner may and a viewer's phone is refused. The printer itself is told nothing. Documented in `docs/LAN_API.md`; the desktop does not serve it yet.
- **Mac: a paired phone carries a role, and the Mac enforces it on every request.** Phone pairing design, decided Nov 22.
- **Mac: "Show prices in OrcaSlicer" and a price grant per slicer, on Connected apps (hidden until "Pair a slicer" is switched on).** A switch at the top of Connected apps turns the Khayt tab's price on or off for every slicer; it starts off. While it is on, each paired slicer has a "Prices" choice: None (the default), Price, or Price and cost. Each choice says what the device learns, and Price says that by trying different plates a device can estimate your material costs. A slicer's row says what it sees. Only the owner can change the switch or a grant; a manager sees them and is told "Only the owner can change this." Price and cost also needs the right to see reports. Both checks are in the writes, not only on the controls. Turning the switch off keeps each grant. Figma: Mac file, page 24. Tests: nobody signed in, a viewer, an operator and a manager can change neither the switch nor a grant; an unknown grant is refused; a phone never holds one. 12 new strings and one changed, in 9 languages.
- **Mac and shared rule: the OrcaSlicer price answer says more about the margin and the rounding (still off; not visible yet).** `lib/connector-price.js priceSlice` now gives the margin three ways (`margin: {pct, pctOnCost, amount}`: of the price, on the cost, and in money), and the step a price was rounded to (`round: {step}`), only when it was rounded. The Mac's route (`POST /api/connectors/price`) passes the margin only to a device granted "Price and cost". The step goes to a device granted "Price" too, since it says nothing of the cost. The route's allow-list is now nested: a key the rule adds later inside `cost`, `margin` or `round` is not passed on until somebody decides who may see it. Existing fields are unchanged. Tests: the 15 shared vectors carry the new fields, a route test per grant, and the nested allow-list.
### Fixed
- **Mac: four fixes from the beta.43 release review.** A paired phone's request that names the same field twice (`{"status":"pending","status":null}`) is now refused: the Mac's role check and the change it made read such a body differently, so an operator's phone could price a job or move a quote on, which only a manager may do. A phone's pause, stop and "bed is clear" now obey the shop's own per-printer limits (Roles ▸ Printers), as the Mac's own buttons do. "An update is ready" is shown even when another sheet was open the moment an update was found (it could stay hidden until a restart, with the update held); it now waits for that sheet to close, and **Check for Updates…** always brings it back. Failed accounting pushes wait while the shop makes no internet calls, as webhook retries do. And "bed is clear" refuses an API token, as the other phone-only routes do.
- **Mac: a phone that knows a newer "keep" purpose than the Mac is no longer refused every time it flips "Make no internet calls".** The Mac compares the kept list the phone was showing with its own, and it never shows a phone a purpose it does not know. A purpose ticked by a newer desktop app and read there by a newer phone therefore never matched, and each request was answered "changed". Purposes the Mac does not show are now left out of that comparison, and still left as they are in the book. Found by the iPhone lane's review.
- **Mac: "you are signed out" is signed.** A phone that hears `device-revoked` drops its key and its copy of the book, and until now anything on the Wi-Fi could say it. The refusal now carries the same reply signature as the role answers, under the key the phone had, and only when the request itself came from that phone. The Mac keeps a signed-out phone's old key for this alone; it opens nothing.
- **Mac: a file sent to Khayt gets a name that is safe on Windows too, and an upload padded with megabytes of spaces is refused at once.** A file's name loses `< > " | ? *` and any dot or space at its end, and a Windows device name (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`…) gets a `_` in front, so a file taken on the Mac can be opened if it ever reaches a Windows computer. The slicer upload reader allows 64 bytes of padding after a part's delimiter, as the Windows/Linux app's does. The Mac's reader never had that app's cost (it reads a saved body once and copies nothing); the limit keeps the two refusing the same request.
- **Mac: an install link to a connector that needs a newer Khayt is refused, and nothing is downloaded.** The list of connectors can say a version needs a newer Khayt (or a newer data format). An update already respected that; a `khayt://plugin/install` link did not, and went on to fetch the connector. It now says "needs a newer Khayt than this one" first, by the same shared rule (`lib/plugin-update.js planUpdate`).
- **Mac: what you do on the Mac is logged under the person signed in on the Mac.** The activity log, and a return's "reported by", read the book's `activeOperatorId` to name who did something. That field is the Windows/Linux app's sign-in, so a job moved on the Mac could be logged under whoever was signed in on another computer. The Mac now credits its own signed-in person, and nobody when the staff lock is off or the change came from a phone, an API token, a recurring order or a customer's answer on the portal. Nothing already in the log is changed.
- **Filament per head goes on the right job, once (shared rule, Mac).** Three faults in how a finished print's per-head figures found their job. An earlier run of the same file could be taken for this print, so one print landed on two jobs and the second job's real figures were refused for good: the run is now the closest one within twenty minutes that no job already holds, and a run another job holds is refused at the write. A print that was not a job's (a calibration started at the printer's screen) could land on the only job printing there: the figures now take only a job that is printing on that machine and names the file, with no fallback; a job names the file by a part's file or by a send that uploaded it under that name, which Khayt now records (`printRuns[].sentAs`), because a file Khayt sends is renamed on the printer. And a printer's run id is held to a short plain token and every figure to a real number, or nothing is written. The rules are `lib/printer-actuals.js` `actualsJob`, `historyRun` and `perHeadActuals`.
- **Mac: filament per head is recorded when nobody is signed in.** With the staff lock on and nobody signed in, which is how the Mac starts, a finished print's per-head figures were refused as if a person had tried to edit the job, and lost. They are the printer's own record and are now written whoever is or is not at the Mac.
